system_description.narrative_title: Iran maritime attacks, Gulf escalation, and mediation
system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative is an escalating campaign of Iranian maritime attacks on commercial tankers in the Strait of Hormuz that is disrupting shipping, driving oil-price and supply-risk reactions, and prompting regional security alarms and evacuations. As an open system this links material flows (oil, ships), force (naval strikes, military posture, evacuations), information/signals (Qatari mediation, US messaging, claims of responsibility) and market responses in recursive feedback loops where attacks raise prices and provoke diplomatic and military reactions that can either dampen or amplify further violence.
system_description.scope: Iranian IRGC naval operations and strikes on tankers; commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz; Gulf states' security responses (Saudi, UAE, Qatar); mediators and diplomatic channels (Qatari negotiators, US envoys); US military posture, evacuations and policy signaling; international oil markets, shipping firms and storage responses; related regional conflicts (Yemen/Houthi activity).
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical and energy system (international security, commerce, and oil markets).
adjacent_subsystems: Gulf regional security architecture (GCC states, UAE, Saudi Arabia)
U.S. domestic politics and military decision-making
Yemen conflict and non-state maritime actors (Houthis)
evidence_headlines: Iran's IRGC Navy says three tankers catch fire in Strait of Hormuz
Qatari negotiators return to Tehran in last-ditch mediation effort
US orders non-emergency staff to leave Saudi Arabia over security risks
Oil Prices Rise After Hormuz Tanker Attack, Houthi Claims Stoke Supply Fears
Iran warns it will retaliate without 'geographical limitations' if attacked
Tankers defy sharp escalation of Iranian attacks to keep crude oil flowing through Strait of Hormuz

variables.name: Maritime attack rate
variables.description: The frequency and intensity of hostile actions directed at commercial vessels in the maritime chokepoint per unit time.

variables.name: Commercial shipping throughput
variables.description: The volumetric or tonnage flow of commercial maritime traffic transiting the chokepoint over time.

variables.name: Oil price level
variables.description: The prevailing market price per barrel of crude oil as reflected in benchmark indexes.

variables.name: Supply-risk perception
variables.description: The aggregate market and stakeholder assessment of the probability and expected severity of oil supply disruptions.

variables.name: Regional military posture
variables.description: The overall level of naval and military deployment, readiness, and aggressive posture in the maritime region.

variables.name: Evacuation and relocation rate
variables.description: The rate at which non-essential personnel and civilians are withdrawn or relocated from at-risk facilities and areas.

variables.name: Diplomatic mediation intensity
variables.description: The level of active mediation and diplomatic engagement aimed at de-escalation across relevant diplomatic channels.

variables.name: Claims and signaling rate
variables.description: The frequency of public claims, communiqués, or rhetoric that signal responsibility or intent around maritime incidents.

variables.name: Shipping insurance premium level
variables.description: The prevailing cost level of insurance coverage for commercial shipping transiting the high-risk maritime area.

variables.name: Shipping rerouting extent
variables.description: The aggregate increase in route distance, time, or volume shifted to alternative pathways due to disruptions.

variables.name: Oil storage utilization
variables.description: The proportion of available onshore and offshore crude oil storage capacity that is filled and operational.

variables.name: Market volatility
variables.description: The short-term variability in prices and trading conditions in oil and related commodity and financial markets.

variables.name: Port and terminal operational disruption
variables.description: The degree to which ports, terminals, and loading/unloading operations are constrained or closed due to security or damage.

variables.name: Maritime environmental damage
variables.description: The extent and severity of environmental contamination and ecological harm from oil spills and related incidents.

variables.name: Conflict spillover risk
variables.description: The assessed probability that localized maritime attacks will expand into broader regional or cross-domain conflict.

variables.name: Maritime security enforcement capacity
variables.description: The aggregate capability of maritime security actors to patrol, interdict, escort, and protect commercial shipping in the area.

catalysts.title: Qatari mediation push in Tehran
catalysts.description: Qatari negotiators' return to Tehran and talks aimed at restarting U.S.–Iran negotiations increase active diplomacy and de-escalation efforts.
catalysts.rationale: "Qatari negotiators return to Tehran"; "Qatari mediators held talks in Tehran aimed at restarting direct U.S.-Iran negotiations."

catalysts.title: Possible post-midterms U.S. strikes
catalysts.description: U.S. warnings about a short, intense renewal of war after midterms imply a heightened risk of strikes or punitive operations in the coming weeks.
catalysts.rationale: "U.S. Warns Gulf of Possible Short, Intense Renewal of Iran War After Midterms"; "U.S. Evacuates Mideast Outposts..."

catalysts.title: Iran tactical shift to limpet mines
catalysts.description: Reports of limpet-mine and mine strikes on tankers indicate a tactical shift that can sustain or intensify maritime attacks on commercial shipping.
catalysts.rationale: "Tanker in Strait of Hormuz hit by limpet mines"; "Iran hits Hormuz tanker with limpet mines in apparent tactical shift."

catalysts.title: Evacuation of non-essential personnel
catalysts.description: U.S. orders and evacuations of non-emergency staff and outposts signal an ongoing withdrawal wave of diplomatic and civilian personnel from high-risk areas.
catalysts.rationale: "US orders non-emergency staff to leave Saudi Arabia"; "U.S. Evacuates Mideast Outposts After Suspected Iranian Plot..."

catalysts.title: Oil spills wash up on UAE beaches
catalysts.description: Spills from tanker attacks are washing ashore in the UAE, creating acute environmental damage and potential port/terminal disruptions and cleanup operations.
catalysts.rationale: "Oil spills from Iran’s tanker attacks wash up on UAE beaches"

catalysts.title: Gulf oil giants expand overseas storage
catalysts.description: Regional oil firms expanding overseas storage capacity as a buffer against war-related supply risk will shift stock placement and affect market perceptions.
catalysts.rationale: "Gulf Oil Giants Work to Expand Overseas Storage As War Exposes Supply Risks"

catalysts.title: U.S. military posture for long stand-off
catalysts.description: U.S. statements and briefings indicating preparedness for a long stand-off imply sustained or increased deployments and readiness in the Gulf.
catalysts.rationale: "US is prepared for long stand-off with Iran"; "Top Military Admiral Briefs Trump on Iran Options"

catalysts.title: Tanker transits continue despite attacks
catalysts.description: Reports that tankers are defying escalation to keep crude flowing will moderate throughput losses but may sustain tensions and reduce rerouting.
catalysts.rationale: "Tankers defy sharp escalation of Iranian attacks to keep crude oil flowing through Strait of Hormuz"
